subject.title: Manual context clearing for tool results

question: Should OpenClaw add caller-directed tool-result clearing as destructive transcript rewrite, model-context-only masking, or recoverable archival, and which CLI, agent, and tool-call adapters should expose that contract?
rationale: This adds core lifecycle/API semantics that affect session replay, persistence, compaction, authorization, and agent control, so automation should not choose the product and safety semantics.

options.title: Design Canonical Archive/Clear Contract
options.body: Define a single lifecycle operation with stable ids, auth, persistence, recovery, and replay semantics before adding CLI or agent-facing adapters.

options.title: Keep Automatic Pruning Only
options.body: Decline manual clearing for now and improve docs or heuristics around TTL, truncation, /compact, /new, and /reset.

options.title: Implement Narrow Destructive Clear
options.body: Add only a targeted clear-by-id operation, accepting that recovery and audit semantics are intentionally minimal.

recommendation.title: Design Canonical Archive/Clear Contract
recommendation.body: Define a single lifecycle operation with stable ids, auth, persistence, recovery, and replay semantics before adding CLI or agent-facing adapters.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored cache-TTL pruning mode and is the strongest adjacent owner for choosing whether manual clearing should extend, replace, or stay separate from the current pruning behavior.
